text:
[IRET.11.3.3] **The identity tiebreak is required for
confluence.** Keying refraction by token hash alone lets
two *distinct* activations whose tokens collide on the
32-bit hash cross-suppress: the second is wrongly treated
as already-fired and its RHS never runs. Because a
from-scratch (batched) build restarts fact ids at 0 — so
its small ids yield small, collision-prone hashes, while
the incremental engine's spread ids rarely collide — this
made the batched result derive *fewer* facts than the
incremental one, violating the batched-equals-incremental
determinism contract (`[LDET.5]`). The fact-id tiebreak
restores it.

The tiebreak applies under every capability setting, the
pooled strategy of `constspace` and `realtime` included
([LDET.1.12]). There the runtime captures the fact-id tuple
in a fixed-size buffer: a token's fact count is bounded by
the network, so capturing it allocates nothing.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__network_agrees
idris.note: Batched equals incremental in order on the instance: the replay is the from-scratch build.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__order_after_history
idris.note: The batched-equals-incremental contract for order, after any history.

idris.name: ldet_5_9__ordered_recompute
idris.note: Batched equals incremental in order: the terminal's order is the canonical order of its recompute, which a from-scratch build produces directly.

idris.name: idat_6_2_2__marked_fired
idris.note: Identity as the fact-id tuple makes the marked activation unique: with distinct identities no other activation is suppressed by the mark.
